
# Avoiding SQL Injection

Never build SQL queries using string concatenation:

```java
//  Very dangerous
String sql = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + username + "'";
```

Instead, always use **`PreparedStatement`**:

```java
PreparedStatement ps = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?");
ps.setString(1, username);
```

This protects against SQL injection attacks and improves performance.

# Automatically Generated IDs

If a table's primary key is generated by the database, leave the ID column out of the `INSERT` statement. PostgreSQL can define an automatically generated ID with an identity column:

```sql
CREATE TABLE students (
    id INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    age INTEGER,
    email VARCHAR(255)
);
```

Insert the student's other values without specifying `id`:

```java
String sql = "INSERT INTO students (name, age, email) VALUES (?, ?, ?)";

try (PreparedStatement ps = conn.prepareStatement(sql, Statement.RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS)) {
    ps.setString(1, "Daniel");
    ps.setInt(2, 24);
    ps.setString(3, "daniel@example.com");

    int rowsInserted = ps.executeUpdate();
    if (rowsInserted != 1) {
        throw new SQLException("Expected one inserted student, but got " + rowsInserted);
    }

    try (ResultSet keys = ps.getGeneratedKeys()) {
        if (keys.next()) {
            int generatedId = keys.getInt(1);
            System.out.println("New student ID: " + generatedId);
        } else {
            throw new SQLException("The database did not return a generated ID");
        }
    }
}
```

The database assigns the ID when the row is inserted. `Statement.RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS` asks JDBC to make generated values available, and `getGeneratedKeys()` retrieves them. Do not include the `id` column in the `INSERT` unless you intentionally want to provide an ID yourself.

## If you don't have identity
You can add identity later if you run query:
```sql
ALTER TABLE students
ALTER COLUMN id ADD GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY;
```
* GENERATED -> Doesn't let user give an ID
* BY DEFAULT -> If user provides an ID, it will accept.

### Note
Don't forget to set the identity to your latest id in the table:
```sql
ALTER TABLE students
ALTER COLUMN id RESTART WITH 43;
```


# Other databases
PostgreSQL -> IDENTITY
SQL Server -> IDENTITY
MySQL   -> AUTO_INCREMENT
Oracle -> IDENTITY
SQLite -> INTEGER Primary Key
